content: No evil can happen to a good man, either in life or after death.
author: Plato
story:
At its core, this reflection cuts through our everyday excuses. Reminding yourself of your mortality is not morbid; it is the most clarifying lens available to human consciousness. When you remember that your days are strictly numbered, petty resentments and trivial anxieties evaporate.

Across his life and work, Plato saw how easily we surrender our tranquility to fear, vanity, and distraction. Death gives urgency and sweetness to every ordinary afternoon. Because this day will never come again, the way you spend your attention right now is of monumental significance.
reflectionPrompt: What quiet yearning in your heart is asking for your attention and honest devotion?
